title: Midwestern backyard birds
subtitle: 26 birds you'll see at feeders, in yards and in parks
description: Each bird as you'd see it perched, then the other plumage: the female, or the winter or juvenile look.

cards.name: Northern cardinal
cards.subtitle: Cardinalis cardinalis
cards.summary: The all-red bird with a crest and a black mask. State bird of seven states.

cues.overall: Bright red with a pointed crest and black face
cues.female: Warm tan-brown with red tinges and a red bill

cards.name: Blue jay
cards.subtitle: Cyanocitta cristata
cards.summary: A loud, crested blue bird that can mimic hawk calls.

cues.overall: Blue crest and back, white belly, black necklace
cues.female: Looks the same as the male

cards.name: American robin
cards.subtitle: Turdus migratorius
cards.summary: The orange-breasted lawn bird that runs, stops, and pulls up worms.

cues.overall: Gray-brown back, brick-orange breast, white eye ring
cues.female: Paler, more washed-out orange breast

cards.name: American goldfinch
cards.subtitle: Spinus tristis
cards.summary: A tiny lemon-yellow finch with black wings that flies in a bouncing wave.

cues.overall: Bright yellow with a black cap and black wings
cues.female: Dull olive-yellow; in winter both sexes turn drab tan

cards.name: House finch
cards.subtitle: Haemorhous mexicanus
cards.summary: A small streaky finch whose male has a raspberry-red head and chest.

cues.overall: Red head and breast, brown-streaked belly and back
cues.female: Plain brown with blurry streaks all over

cards.name: Black-capped chickadee
cards.subtitle: Poecile atricapillus
cards.summary: A tiny, fearless bird with a black cap and bib that says its own name.
facts: Thousands of seeds to eat later

cues.overall: Black cap and bib, white cheeks, gray back
cues.female: Looks the same as the male

cards.name: Tufted titmouse
cards.subtitle: Baeolophus bicolor
cards.summary: A small gray bird with a crest and big black eyes.

cues.overall: Soft gray crest and back, peach flanks
cues.female: Looks the same as the male

cards.name: White-breasted nuthatch
cards.subtitle: Sitta carolinensis
cards.summary: The bird that walks headfirst down tree trunks.

cues.overall: Blue-gray back, white face and breast, black cap
cues.female: Cap is gray instead of black

cards.name: Downy woodpecker
cards.subtitle: Dryobates pubescens
cards.summary: The smallest woodpecker, with a tiny bill; regular at suet feeders.
facts: Short, much shorter than its head

cues.overall: Black and white with a red patch on the back of the head
cues.female: No red patch

cards.name: Red-bellied woodpecker
cards.subtitle: Melanerpes carolinus
cards.summary: A zebra-backed woodpecker with a red cap; the red belly is barely visible.

cues.overall: Barred back, red cap from bill to nape
cues.female: Red only on the nape, gray crown

cards.name: Northern flicker
cards.subtitle: Colaptes auratus
cards.summary: A brown, spotted woodpecker that feeds on the ground, eating ants.
facts: Flashes yellow underwings and white rump

cues.overall: Brown with black spots, black bib, red nape
cues.female: No black 'mustache' stripe

cards.name: Mourning dove
cards.subtitle: Zenaida macroura
cards.summary: A slim tan dove whose soft, sad cooing gives it its name.

cues.overall: Soft tan-gray with black spots on wings, long pointed tail
cues.female: Slightly browner, less pink and blue

cards.name: Dark-eyed junco
cards.subtitle: Junco hyemalis
cards.summary: The 'snowbird': a slate-gray sparrow that arrives for winter.
facts: Winter, on the ground under feeders

cues.overall: Slate gray above, white belly, pink bill
cues.female: Browner gray

cards.name: Song sparrow
cards.subtitle: Melospiza melodia
cards.summary: A streaky brown sparrow with a central breast spot and a cheerful song.
facts: Maids, maids, put on your tea-kettle
Streaks gather into a dark spot

cues.overall: Brown streaks on white, dark central spot
cues.female: Looks the same as the male

cards.name: House sparrow
cards.subtitle: Passer domesticus
cards.summary: Not a native: a chunky city sparrow brought from Europe in the 1850s.

cues.overall: Gray cap, chestnut nape, black bib
cues.female: Plain buffy-brown with a pale eye stripe

cards.name: European starling
cards.subtitle: Sturnus vulgaris
cards.summary: An iridescent, speckled import that flies in huge swirling flocks.

cues.overall: Glossy purple-green, yellow bill in spring
cues.female: Winter look: covered in white spots, dark bill

cards.name: Red-winged blackbird
cards.subtitle: Agelaius phoeniceus
cards.summary: The marsh bird singing from cattails, flashing red-and-yellow shoulder patches.
facts: One of the first signs of spring

cues.overall: All black with red and yellow shoulder patches
cues.female: Dark brown and heavily streaked, like a big sparrow

cards.name: Common grackle
cards.subtitle: Quiscalus quiscula
cards.summary: A long-tailed, glossy blackbird with staring yellow eyes.

cues.overall: Glossy purple-bronze head, long tail, yellow eye
cues.female: Duller and browner, shorter tail

cards.name: Brown-headed cowbird
cards.subtitle: Molothrus ater
cards.summary: A blackbird that lays its eggs in other birds' nests.
facts: Never: other birds raise its young

cues.overall: Glossy black body, chocolate-brown head
cues.female: Plain gray-brown all over

cards.name: Baltimore oriole
cards.subtitle: Icterus galbula
cards.summary: A flame-orange and black songbird that loves oranges and grape jelly.

cues.overall: Fiery orange with a black head and back
cues.female: Yellow-orange with grayish wings

cards.name: Indigo bunting
cards.subtitle: Passerina cyanea
cards.summary: A small bird of field edges that's blue all over. The color is a trick of the light.
facts: Paired notes: fire, fire, where, where

cues.overall: Deep, electric blue all over
cues.female: Plain warm brown, faint streaks

cards.name: Rose-breasted grosbeak
cards.subtitle: Pheucticus ludovicianus
cards.summary: A black-and-white songbird with a rose-red triangle on its chest.
facts: Like a robin that took voice lessons

cues.overall: Black hood and back, white belly, red chest patch
cues.female: Streaky brown with a bold white eyebrow

cards.name: Ruby-throated hummingbird
cards.subtitle: Archilochus colubris
cards.summary: The only hummingbird nesting in the eastern US; weighs less than a nickel.

cues.overall: Emerald back, flashing ruby-red throat
cues.female: Green back, plain white throat

cards.name: Cedar waxwing
cards.subtitle: Bombycilla cedrorum
cards.summary: A sleek, crested bird with a black mask and a yellow-tipped tail, in berry-eating flocks.

cues.overall: Silky tan, crest, black mask, yellow tail tip
cues.female: Looks nearly the same as the male

cards.name: Carolina wren
cards.subtitle: Thryothorus ludovicianus
cards.summary: A small, round, cocked-tail wren with a huge voice.

cues.overall: Rich brown, buff belly, white eyebrow, cocked tail
cues.female: Looks the same as the male

cards.name: Red-tailed hawk
cards.subtitle: Buteo jamaicensis
cards.summary: The big hawk perched on highway light poles, with a brick-red tail.
facts: Mice and voles from a perch

cues.overall: Pale breast with a dark belly band, rusty tail
cues.female: Same look, but larger; juveniles have a banded brown tail
